docs.title: Helix SSPA Controller
docs.text:
Control and protection for solid-state HF amplifiers. The controller pairs an STM32G474 control board with an ESP32-P4 touch display. It switches bands automatically from your radio, sequences the RX/TX relay and the PA bias, and trips in hardware on SWR, filter reflection, output power, temperature, voltage and current.

This manual covers controller board Rev 4.01 with firmware 105 (controller and display). Use the version menu at the top to read an older edition.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

The main screen (needle meter face).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Protection in hardware. Fast comparators trip on antenna SWR, LPF SWR, output power, PA temperature, supply voltage and drain current. A latch holds the fault, removes the bias, opens the PA supply switch, inhibits the radio and pulls its ALC down until you reset it.
  • Safe TX sequencing. The RX/TX relay closes first, the bias follows 20 ms later, and on release the bias goes before the relay moves back. A PTT held at power-up or after a fault never keys the amplifier.
  • Automatic band switching from band voltage, BCD, CAT or Icom CI-V, with per-band LPF and antenna maps.
  • Metering: SSB-safe peak-hold PEP and SWR, average power, supply voltage and current, two temperatures and fan speed, on four meter faces.
  • Accessories: 4-way antenna selector with a separate RX antenna, antenna rotator with GS-232B network control, and control of compatible power supplies over CAN.
  • Remote: a browser app on your phone or PC, and an optional second display (remote head) on your network. Firmware updates for both boards over WiFi.

docs.title: System overview
docs.text:

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
The short path from a wired controller to a working amplifier. Do the steps in this order: each one relies on the one before it. Each step links to the full instructions.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

  1. Wire it up. Follow Connectors and wiring, then do the first power-up on 12 V only, with the PA supply off. Check that the display starts.
  2. Set the current sensor. Menu → Power: choose the sensor type of your High Side Switch or power module and enter its values. See Power module.
  3. Set the LPF map. Menu → LPF Map: tell the controller which LPF bank each band uses. See LPF map.
  4. Set the temperature sensors. Menu → Temperature: enter each NTC's resistance and beta, and the fan start and full-speed temperatures. See Temperature and fan.
  5. Set the protection trip levels. Menu → Protection: turn the trimmers for voltage (RV3), current (RV4) and temperature (RV5) until each trip value reads what you want. See Protection.
  6. Calibrate the power meter. Menu → RF Calibrate, with a dummy load and a reference wattmeter. See RF power calibration. Then set the output power trip (RV2) and the LPF SWR trip (RV1).
  7. Choose the band data source (band voltage, BCD, CAT or CI-V) and your radio profile. See Band data and radio.
  8. Map the antennas if you use the antenna selector. See Antenna selection.
  9. Test every protection trip into a dummy load before going on the air. See Test the protection.

Optional: connect the display to your WiFi to use the browser app, the remote head and firmware updates. See Network and remote.

Every settings page has an APPLY button

Changes on a settings page take effect when you tap APPLY. The page then shows Configuration Saved once they are stored. Amplifier settings are kept in the controller board's EEPROM; display, network and CAN settings are kept in the display. Both survive power cycles and firmware updates.

docs.title: Technical reference
docs.text: How the controller is built, with the parts used, for builders and anyone who wants to know what is inside. Figures are for controller board Rev 4.01 and firmware 105.

docs.title: Controller board
docs.text: Processor ST STM32G474VET6, Arm Cortex-M4F at 170 MHz, 512 KB flash, 16 MHz crystal. Chosen for its analog peripherals: five fast 12-bit ADCs, with forward and reflected power sampled at the same instant by two ADCs in dual simultaneous mode. PCB 4-layer, 1.6 mm Supply 12–14 V DC, 5 A resettable fuse, reverse-polarity protection Settings storage CAT24C256 32 KB I²C EEPROM on the controller board. Every amplifier setting is kept here, so it survives firmware updates and never wears out the STM32's internal flash. Settings that change often, such as PA ENABLE, are written only after 5 minutes without a change, to spare the EEPROM as well. Display link 3.3 V UART, 115200 baud; firmware updates for the controller pass over the same link Bootloader 16 KB, CRC-checked firmware images; USB DFU recovery through the processor's ROM bootloader

docs.title: Protection path
docs.text:
The protection does not depend on the processor or the firmware.

  • Comparators: three TLV3502 dual high-speed comparators (4.5 ns propagation delay) watch antenna SWR, LPF SWR, output power, supply voltage, drain current and temperature.
  • Latch: a 74HC74 flip-flop holds the first trip until PA RESET, so a fault that clears by itself still leaves the amplifier off and shows what happened. Comparator plus latch respond in tens of nanoseconds.
  • Fast bias cut-off: the latch drives N-channel MOSFETs (AO3400A) directly, with 33 Ω gate resistors, to switch off the bias switch (AO3401A P-MOSFET) and pull the optional gate-kill line to GND.
  • PA supply: two IRLML0100 100 V MOSFETs give the High Side Switch a fail-safe and an active-on control line.
  • ALC and TX inhibit: on a fault, an ADG419 analog switch pulls the radio's ALC to a negative voltage (from an ICL7660 −12 V charge pump, clamped by Zener diodes to about −4 V and −10 V), so the radio's power goes down as well. TX inhibit is an open-drain AO3400A.
  • Firmware backup: the processor sees every fault on an interrupt and drops the bias and the RX/TX relay within microseconds, independently of the latch. The first fault is timestamped, so the display shows the cause rather than the faults that the trip itself triggers.

docs.title: Inputs and outputs
docs.text:
• Optocouplers: five LTV-217 optocouplers isolate the PTT input and the four BCD band-data inputs, for a large voltage margin and no ground loop to the radio.
  • LPF drivers: two types of LPF board are supported. A2982 8-channel source drivers (outputs switch to +12 V) and a ULN2803A 8-channel sink driver (outputs switch to GND, clamp diodes on board); 500 mA per output.
  • Antenna selector: a second A2982 drives the antenna and spare outputs.
  • Frequency counter input: SN65LVDS2 LVDS receiver.
  • Data line protection: PRTR5V0U2X ESD protection on the display, Neural module and USB lines.

docs.title: EMI and RF immunity
docs.text: Every signal and power line that leaves the board passes through a ferrite bead and an RC filter to ground, to keep RF from the amplifier out of the control circuits.

docs.title: Power supply
docs.text:
A three-stage supply keeps the efficiency high and the heat low:

  1. LMR51430 synchronous buck converter, 12 V to 6.6 V.
  2. MIC29302 3 A low-dropout regulator, 6.6 V to 5 V (display, CAT and band-data supplies).
  3. TLV73333 low-dropout regulator, 3.3 V for the processor and the analog circuits.

The fan and the relay drivers run from separate LC-filtered 12 V rails.

docs.title: Display
docs.text: Processor Espressif ESP32-P4, dual-core RISC-V (rated to 400 MHz; firmware 105 runs it at 360 MHz), 32 MB flash Screen 1024 × 600 pixels, MIPI-DSI, capacitive touch (GT911) WiFi ESP32-C6 co-processor CAN TJA1051 transceiver, 125 kbit/s, 120 Ω termination on board Settings storage Display, network, remote and CAN settings in the display's own non-volatile memory (NVS) Firmware Two firmware slots: a failed or unwanted update can be rolled back

docs.title: Timing
docs.text: Event Time Comparator response 4.5 ns (TLV3502) Key-up: RX/TX relay to bias on 20 ms Key-down: bias off to relay release 5 ms PTT release debounce 2 ms PA RESET pulse to external modules (nRST-RLY) 300 ms Meter update while transmitting 4 per second (power bar 20 per second)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Common problems, what causes them and how to fix them. Two tools help with almost all of them:

  • Diagnose (menu → Diagnose) shows the live reading of every analog input. See Diagnostics.
  • The test points show whether each supply rail is there. See Test points.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

docs.title: Power and display
docs.text: Problem Check Nothing lights, the power LED is off Measure the supply at J22 and at TP5. If TP5 reads 0 V, the supply may be reversed: the input fuse trips. Correct the polarity and wait a minute for the fuse to cool. Power LED on, display stays dark Measure TP1 (5 V). Check the display cable at J18: pin 4 is +5 V, pin 1 GND. A supply rail is missing or low Unplug the connectors one at a time, starting with the display, fan and relay boards. A rail that comes back points to a short or an overload on that connector. The picture is upside down Menu → Display → untick Rotate display, APPLY, and restart.

docs.title: Display and controller not talking
docs.text:
The display and the controller talk over a 3.3 V serial link on J18. The signs of a broken link:

  • Info shows Controller Firmware as 0.
  • Temperatures, voltage and current stay at 0; PA ENABLE and the band buttons do nothing.
  • APPLY never shows Configuration Saved.

TX goes to RX

The controller's TX (J18 pin 3) must go to the display's RX, and the controller's RX (J18 pin 2) to the display's TX. Some display manufacturers label their connector the other way round (from the other end of the cable), so a cable wired "TX to TX" by the labels can be right, and one wired "TX to RX" can be wrong. Check the pin-out in your display's own manual.

If the link does not work, switch everything off and swap the wires on pins 2 and 3. Both lines are 3.3 V logic, so the display must use 3.3 V on its serial port, not 5 V.

Also check:

  • GND (pin 1) is connected at both ends.
  • The cable is short and kept away from the PA output coax.
  • Both boards run firmware of the same release (menu → Info).

docs.title: Keying and the RX/TX relay
docs.text: Problem Check TRANSMIT does not light when you key the radio PA ENABLE must be on (bright green); in standby the amplifier never keys. Check the PTT wiring at J26: the radio's SEND / TX-GND output must pull pin 2 to GND when transmitting. PA ENABLE does not change Press and hold it. It does not change while transmitting or while the protection is latched (PA RESET red). The amplifier does not key after a fault, a reset or power-up Unkey the radio once. The amplifier never keys into a PTT that was already held; it needs a fresh key-down. TRANSMIT lights, but no relay click Measure J26 pin 4: +12 V while transmitting. Check the relay coil and its GND return. The relay chatters on SSB Check the PTT cable for RF pickup: use shielded cable, and fit a ferrite on it at the amplifier end.

docs.title: Protection
docs.text: Problem Check PA RESET does nothing A fault is still present: its indicator is red. Fix the cause first. PA RESET is also refused while transmitting. ANT SWR trips at key-up, even into a dummy load The forward and reflected wires from the antenna bridge may be swapped. In Diagnose, transmit at low power into the dummy load: ANT REF must be far lower than ANT FWD. Also check the coax and the load itself. LPF SWR trips on one band only The LPF map sends that band to the wrong filter, the filter relay does not switch, or the filter is faulty. If all filters are good, RV1 is set too sensitive. CURRENT or VOLTAGE trips at normal power Check the trip value on the Protection page against your operating level, and the current sensor settings (a wrong sensor type makes the reading, and the trip value shown, wrong). TEMP. trips too early Check the NTC values on the Temperature page, and that NTC 1 sits on the heatsink, not on a hot spot such as a resistor. RF IN trips The external drive-protection input (J14 pin 4) is high. Reduce the drive, or check the module that drives this input. If nothing is connected there, check for a short to a supply.

docs.title: Readings
docs.text:
Problem Check Power reads 0 while transmitting The power meter is not calibrated: see RF power calibration. SWR shows -- Normal while receiving. SWR is measured only while transmitting. SWR jumps about at low power The reflected signal is near the detector's noise floor. Read SWR at a higher power. Power reads wrong after calibration Calibrate again with a steady carrier and the wattmeter in the line. LOW, MID and HIGH must increase in order. Current reads negative Tick INVERT MODE on the Power page (shunt and Hall sensors). Current or voltage reads 0 Check the wiring at J8 and the sensor type on the Power page. Voltage or current a little off Correct it with VOLTAGE CALIBRATION / CURRENT CALIBRATION on the Power page. A temperature reads far below room temperature That NTC is open or not connected. A temperature reads very high That NTC or its wiring is shorted. Both temperatures read wrong by a few degrees Enter the correct resistance and beta for your NTCs on the Temperature page.

Check NTC 1 before operating

The hardware over-temperature trip uses NTC 1. If NTC 1 is open or unplugged, it reads very cold and the trip can never fire. Always check that TEMP1 reads a sensible temperature before going on the air.

docs.title: Fan
docs.text:
Problem Check Fan always at full speed 4-wire fan: check the PWM wire on J20 pin 2 (most PC fans run flat out when the PWM wire is open). If the speed falls as the amplifier warms up, tick Invert PWM. Fan never speeds up Check the FAN PWM range on the Temperature page, and that the NTCs read correctly. Fan does not run at all Measure TP4 (fan 12 V). 2-wire fans connect between pins 4 and 3, 4-wire fans between pins 4 and 1.

The fan never stops completely: 10 % is the minimum.

docs.title: Band selection
docs.text: Problem Check The amplifier does not follow the radio's band AUTO BAND must be on (lit). The method on the Band Data page must not be None, and the profile must have a value for that band (a band left at 0 is ignored). It selects the wrong band Band voltage: the windows overlap or are too wide; check LIVE BAND VOLTAGE on each band. BCD: compare LIVE BAND DATA with the ticks for that band. Band data reads 0 on every band Check the band-data cable at J1, and that band data is switched on in the radio's menu. A band button does nothing No band changes while transmitting. In AUTO the radio chooses the band: hold AUTO BAND to switch to manual. The band changes only after unkeying Normal. A band change from the radio during TX is applied when you unkey. APPLY on a band page does nothing just after power-up The display is still receiving the radio profiles from the controller. Wait a few seconds and tap APPLY again.

docs.title: CAT and CI-V
docs.text: Problem Check CAT chip stays off Baud rate (and CI-V address for Icom) must match the radio exactly; do not use Auto baud on the radio. Icom: band follows only when you change it on the amplifier Turn CI-V Transceive on in the radio. No data at all Logic level: solder jumper JP2 must match the radio or interface (5 V or 3.3 V). An RS-232 port (±12 V) needs a level converter. For CI-V use J16 pin 3, not pin 2. Frequency widget shows --.---.--- No CAT or CI-V data. Check the CAT chip first.

docs.title: Antennas and rotator
docs.text: Problem Check The RX antenna relay never switches It works only with PA ENABLE on, while receiving, on a band with RX ANT ticked on the Antenna page. The wrong antenna is selected Check the Antenna page, and the relay order at J45: the TX antennas use a cumulative code, not one wire per antenna. >> turns the rotator the wrong way Swap the two relay wires at J32. The rotator does not move Tick Enable rotator control on the Rotator page. Check the relay supply in the rotator control box. The heading is wrong Redo the 3-point calibration, and check CCW stop heading. Rotator ADC must change smoothly over the whole turn. The rotator stops before the target The position reading stopped changing (a stall or a loose pot wire), or the run took too long. Check the pot wiring and the mechanics.

docs.title: Network and browser app
docs.text: Problem Check helixrf-sspa4.local does not open Use the IP address shown on the Network page instead. Some phones (Android in particular) do not find .local names. The PC or phone must be on the same network. The page opens but shows no data Enable browser app must be ticked (menu → Remote). Check that AIRPLANE MODE is off. The dot shows not live The browser lost the connection: check the WiFi signal on the Info page, and reload the page. The remote head does not connect Tick Enable remote display head, then tap PAIR and confirm the code shown on the head. A rotator program cannot connect The rotator must be enabled. Use port 4001. Only one program can connect at a time.

docs.title: CAN power supply
docs.text: Problem Check CAN chip stays off Choose the supply under CONNECTED MODULE. Check CAN-H and CAN-L (not swapped), GND, and the 120 Ω termination at the supply end. CAN chip on, but no readings The supply is on the bus but not answering. Choose None, then choose the supply again: that restarts discovery. Flatpack2 telemetry disappears for about 20 s after APPLY Normal: the supply is storing the new default voltage.

docs.title: Firmware update
docs.text: Problem Check The update page refuses to start Stop transmitting. The controller file is rejected Use controller4-vNNN.bin, not the _full.bin (that one is for USB recovery only). The controller update stopped part way Open the Firmware Update page again and click Retry flashing. The controller waits in its bootloader until it gets a good image. The controller does not start at all Recover it over USB: see Recovering the controller. The new display firmware misbehaves Use the Restore display4-vNNN button on the Firmware Update page.

docs.text: Note what you see (the indicators, the Info page versions and a photo of the Diagnose page help a lot) and request free remote support. We connect to your station PC and help you get on the air.

How to wire the controller into your amplifier and check it before the PA supply is ever switched on.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A 12 V DC supply for the controller (see J22).
  • JST PH (2.0 mm) housings and crimp contacts, or wire for the solder pads.
  • Shielded cable or twisted pairs for the SWR bridge signals.
  • A multimeter.
  • A dummy load rated for the full output power, and a reference wattmeter for the power calibration.
  • A small screwdriver for the protection trimmers (RV1–RV5).

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Wire the modules to the controller as shown in Connectors and wiring. It has the system diagrams, and a pin-out and wiring sketch for every connector.

Suggested order:

  1. 12 V supply (J22) and the display (J18).
  2. High Side Switch: sense (J8) and control (J10).
  3. LPF module: power (J39) and band select (J43 or J41).
  4. SWR bridges (J3, J5), NTCs (J28) and fan (J20).
  5. PTT and RX/TX relay (J26), PA bias (J30).
  6. Radio band data (J1 or J16), ALC and TX inhibit (J24), and the optional antenna selector (J45) and rotator (J32).

Connectors and wiring →

docs.title: First power-up
docs.text:
Do this with the PA supply switched off and no drive from the radio.

  1. Before connecting the board, measure the 12 V supply: check its polarity and that it reads 12–14 V.
  2. Connect the 12 V supply and the display only. The power LED on the controller board lights, and the display shows the HelixRF splash screen, then the main screen. Measure the supply rails at the test points.
  3. Swipe down to open the menu and tap Info. Controller Firmware shows a version number when the display and the controller are talking. If it stays at 0, check the display cable (J18): the controller's TX must go to the display's RX. See Display and controller not talking.
  4. Connect the rest of the wiring (power off while you plug in).
  5. Power up again and open Diagnose. Check that both NTCs give a plausible reading and that nothing reads full scale (4095) with no signal applied. See Diagnostics.
  6. On the main screen, press and hold PA ENABLE until it turns bright green. (The PA supply is still off.)
  7. Key the radio with its power at zero. TRANSMIT lights at the top right and you hear the RX/TX relay change over. Unkey: the relay drops. With PA ENABLE off the relay stays in receive: that is the standby mode.

Test the relay before connecting the drive

Check that the relay changes over on PTT with no RF applied, before you connect the drive cable.

docs.title: Test points
docs.text:
Seven test pads on the top of the controller board give quick access to every supply rail. Measure them with a multimeter against GND (for example J22 pin 1). The silkscreen label next to each pad is shown in brackets.

Test points on the top of the controller board. Click to enlarge. Test point Rail Expected Supplies TP5 (R12v) +12 V input, after fuse F1 Your supply voltage Everything below TP6 (L12v) +12 V, filtered Your supply voltage LPF and antenna relay drivers, RX/TX relay TP4 (F12v) +12 V fan, filtered Your supply voltage Fan connector J20 TP2 (6v6) +6.6 V 6.6 V Buck converter output, feeds the 5 V regulator TP1 (5v) +5 V 5.0 V Display, CAT, band-data and Neural supplies TP3 (3v3) +3.3 V 3.3 V Processor, comparators, logic TP7 (12v) −12 V Negative, close to your supply voltage ALC switch, pinch-off supply (J30 pin 6)

If TP5 reads 0 V, check the supply polarity: the input fuse trips when the supply is reversed. If TP5 is fine but a lower rail is missing, the stage that makes it, or something loading it, is at fault. Disconnect the connectors one at a time to find the load.

Then work through the setup in the order given in Getting started.

docs.title: Connectors and wiring
docs.text:
Every connector on the controller board, what it does, its pin-out and how to wire it. Pin numbers follow the board silkscreen; pin 1 is GND on almost every connector.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

Two footprints per connector

Most connectors appear twice on the board under two reference numbers, for example J3 / J4. The first is a JST PH (2.0 mm) side-entry socket, the second is a row of solder pads wired in parallel. Use whichever suits your build: a crimped JST PH lead, or wires soldered straight to the pads. Never use both at once.

docs.title: J22 / J23 · 12 V power in
docs.text:
The 12 V logic supply for the controller, the display, the fan and all relay outputs.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 +12 V In 12–14 V DC (13.8 V is fine). Do not exceed 15 V.

The input is protected by a 5 A resettable fuse (F1) and a reverse-polarity diode: connected the wrong way round, the fuse trips and the board stays off. Size the supply for the board and display plus your fan and every relay coil that can be on at the same time (one LPF relay, up to four antenna relays and the RX/TX relay).

The 52 V PA supply never goes to the controller board. It runs through the High Side Switch module (see the Power diagram above).

docs.title: J10 / J11 · PSU protection
docs.text:
Turns the 52 V PA supply off when the hardware protection latches a fault. Pins 2 and 3 are open-drain outputs (MOSFET to GND) with opposite sense, so the switch module can use whichever its gate driver needs.

Pin Signal Direction Normal operation Fault latched 1 GND 2 ~PROT-VCC Out Open Switched to GND 3 PROT-VCC Out Switched to GND Open 4 +3.3 V Out Supply for the switch logic
  • Use pin 3 for a switch that stays on only while its control input is held to GND. This is fail-safe: a broken wire turns the PA supply off.
  • Use pin 2 for a switch that turns off when its control input is pulled to GND.

The High Side Switch manual shows which pin it uses.

docs.title: J30 / J31 · PA bias
docs.text:
Switches the pallet's gate bias. The controller applies bias only while transmitting, after the RX/TX relay has settled (20 ms), and removes it 5 ms before the relay returns to receive. A protection fault removes it at once, in hardware.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 BIAS-IN In Bias supply from the pallet, up to 12 V 3 BIAS-OUT Out Switched bias back to the pallet's gate-bias input 4 Gate kill (optional) Out Open drain: pulled to GND while a fault is latched 5 +12 V Out Low-current supply for an external pinch-off circuit 6 −12 V Out Low-current supply for an external pinch-off circuit 7 PINCH Out Logic high (3.3 V) while a fault is latched 8 BIAS_CTRL Out Logic high while transmitting, for pallets with a bias-enable input

Most LDMOS pallets need only pins 1–3: break the pallet's bias supply line and route it through BIAS-IN and BIAS-OUT. Pins 4–8 are for pallets that need a hard gate kill, a negative pinch-off voltage or a separate bias-enable signal.

 Controller J30                     RF pallet
 ┌───────────────┐                 ┌──────────────────┐
 │ 2  BIAS-IN    │◄────────────────┤ bias supply out  │
 │ 3  BIAS-OUT   ├────────────────►│ gate bias in     │
 │ 4  Gate kill  ├ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─►│ gate (optional)  │
 │ 8  BIAS_CTRL  ├ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─►│ bias enable (opt)│
 │ 1  GND        ├─────────────────┤ GND              │
 └───────────────┘                 └──────────────────┘
       ─── required    ─ ─ optional

docs.title: J3 / J4 and J5 / J6 · SWR bridges
docs.text:
DC outputs from the two directional couplers. J3 / J4 reads the bridge on the antenna side (after the LPF). J5 / J6 reads the bridge between the PA and the LPF, which catches a wrong or failed filter. Both feed the hardware SWR trips; the antenna bridge also drives the power and SWR meters.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 Reflected (ANT-R / LPF-R) In DC from the reflected detector 3 GND 4 Forward (ANT-F / LPF-F) In DC from the forward detector

Use shielded cable or a twisted pair per signal, and keep it away from the PA output coax.

 SWR bridge                         Controller J3 (antenna) / J5 (LPF)
 ┌──────────────┐                  ┌──────────────┐
 │ FWD detector ├─────────────────►│ 4  FWD       │
 │          GND ├──────────────────┤ 3  GND       │
 │ REF detector ├─────────────────►│ 2  REF       │
 │          GND ├──────────────────┤ 1  GND       │
 └──────────────┘                  └──────────────┘

Calibrate the meter after wiring; see RF power calibration.

docs.title: J28 / J29 · NTC temperature sensors
docs.text:
Two NTC thermistors. The fan speed follows whichever reads higher. The hardware over-temperature trip watches NTC 1 only, so mount NTC 1 on the pallet heatsink, next to the transistor. NTC 2 can go on the LPF, the combiner or the PSU.

Each NTC sits between +3.3 V and its sense pin; the board has a 10 kΩ resistor from each sense pin to GND.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 +3.3 V Out NTC 1 supply 2 NTC-1 In NTC 1 sense (heatsink; used by the hardware trip) 3 +3.3 V Out NTC 2 supply 4 NTC-2 In NTC 2 sense

Use 10 kΩ NTCs. The firmware defaults to 10 kΩ at 25 °C and β = 3950, the values of the common 10 kΩ "3950" thermistor. For a different NTC, enter its resistance and beta on the display; see Temperature and fan.

 Controller J28
 ┌──────────────┐        NTC 1 (pallet heatsink)
 │ 1  +3.3V     ├────────/\/\/\────┐
 │ 2  NTC-1     ├──────────────────┘
 │              │        NTC 2
 │ 3  +3.3V     ├────────/\/\/\────┐
 │ 4  NTC-2     ├──────────────────┘
 └──────────────┘

docs.title: J20 / J21 · Fan
docs.text:
Variable fan speed. The speed ramps from 10 % at the "fan low" temperature to 100 % at "fan high"; the fan never stops completely. Two-wire fans are switched on their negative lead; four-wire PC fans take the PWM signal.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 PWM Out PWM control for 4-wire fans 3 FAN − Out Switched negative for 2-wire fans 4 +12 V Out Fan supply (filtered) 2-wire fan4-wire PC fan 
 Controller J20                 Fan
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌──────────┐
 │ 4  +12V      ├──────────────┤ + (red)  │
 │ 3  FAN −     ├──────────────┤ − (black)│
 └──────────────┘              └──────────┘

 Controller J20                 Fan
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌──────────────┐
 │ 4  +12V      ├──────────────┤ +12V (yellow)│
 │ 1  GND       ├──────────────┤ GND  (black) │
 │ 2  PWM       ├──────────────┤ PWM  (blue)  │
 └──────────────┘              └──────────────┘
   (tach wire not used)

If the fan runs backwards to the temperature (fast when cold), turn on Invert PWM on the Temperature page.

docs.title: J41 / J42 and J43 / J44 · LPF band select
docs.text:
Eight band outputs to the LPF relay board, one per filter bank. Exactly one output is on at a time. Which bank each band uses is set in the LPF map. The outputs are given twice, so you can use whichever matches your relay board:

  • J43 / J44 (LPF): sourcing. The active pin goes to +12 V. Wire each relay coil between the pin and GND.
  • J41 / J42 (~LPF): sinking. The active pin goes to GND (open collector). Wire each relay coil between +12 V and the pin.
Pin J43 / J44 (sourcing) J41 / J42 (sinking) 1 BAND1 ~BAND1 2 BAND2 ~BAND2 3 BAND3 ~BAND3 4 BAND4 ~BAND4 5 BAND5 ~BAND5 6 BAND6 ~BAND6 7 BAND7 ~BAND7 8 BAND8 ~BAND8

The drivers (A2982 sourcing, ULN2803A sinking) are rated 500 mA per output; keep each relay coil well below that. The sinking outputs have clamp diodes on the board. For the sourcing outputs, fit a flyback diode across each relay coil on the LPF board.

Sourcing (J43)Sinking (J41) 
 Controller J43                 LPF module (one bank shown)
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌────────────────────────┐
 │ 1  BAND1     ├─────────────►│ relay coil ──┐         │
 │ …            │              │              GND       │
 │ 8  BAND8     ├─────────────►│ (one per bank)         │
 └──────────────┘              └────────────────────────┘
 Power the LPF board from J39 (+12 V and GND).

 Controller J41                 LPF module (one bank shown)
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌────────────────────────┐
 │ 1  ~BAND1    ├──────────────┤ relay coil ── +12V     │
 │ …            │              │                        │
 │ 8  ~BAND8    ├──────────────┤ (one per bank)         │
 └──────────────┘              └────────────────────────┘
 Relay +12 V comes from J39.

docs.title: J45 / J46 · Antenna selector
docs.text:
Drives the optional 4-way antenna selector and a separate receive-antenna relay. All outputs are sourcing (+12 V when on, A2982 driver, 500 mA per output). The TX antenna is chosen per band on the display and never changes while transmitting.

Pin Signal Notes 1 ANT1 TX antenna relay 1 2 ANT2 TX antenna relay 2 3 ANT3 TX antenna relay 3 4 ANT4 Dedicated RX antenna relay 5–8 EX1–EX4 Spare sourcing outputs, not used by firmware 105

The TX antenna relays use a cumulative code, so a cascade of three changeover relays selects four antennas:

Antenna ANT1 ANT2 ANT3 ANT 1 (default, no relay on) off off off ANT 2 on off off ANT 3 on on off ANT 4 on on on

The RX antenna relay (ANT4) is on only while receiving, with PA ENABLE on, on a band set to use the RX antenna. It drops the moment the amplifier keys.

J45 has no GND pin. Return the relay coils to GND at the selector board, taking GND from J39 or the chassis. Fit a flyback diode across each coil.

 Controller J45                     Antenna selector board
 ┌──────────────┐                  ┌─────────────────────────┐
 │ 1  ANT1      ├─────────────────►│ K1 coil ─┐              │
 │ 2  ANT2      ├─────────────────►│ K2 coil ─┤  coils to    │
 │ 3  ANT3      ├─────────────────►│ K3 coil ─┤  GND         │
 │ 4  ANT4 (RX) ├─────────────────►│ RX relay─┘              │
 └──────────────┘                  └─────────────────────────┘

docs.title: J26 / J27 · PTT and RX/TX relay
docs.text:
Keying input from the radio and the drive for the RX/TX changeover relay. The controller sequences the relay and the bias so the relay never switches with RF present.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 ~PTT In Active low: radio's TX-GND / SEND output pulls it to GND 3 nRST-RLY Out Open drain: pulled to GND for 300 ms when you press PA RESET 4 RX/TX RLY Out +12 V while transmitting; flyback diode on board

nRST-RLY resets external modules that latch their own faults. Wire it to the module's reset input (active low), or leave it unconnected.

 Radio                Controller J26              RX/TX relay
 ┌──────────┐        ┌──────────────┐            ┌──────────┐
 │ SEND/PTT ├───────►│ 2  ~PTT      │            │          │
 │      GND ├────────┤ 1  GND       ├────────────┤ coil −   │
 └──────────┘        │ 4  RX/TX RLY ├───────────►│ coil +   │
                     └──────────────┘            └──────────┘

Test before going on the air

Check that the relay changes over on PTT with no RF applied, before you connect the drive cable.

docs.title: J24 / J25 · ALC and TX inhibit
docs.text:
Protection outputs to the radio. While a fault is latched, the controller pulls the radio's ALC negative and asserts TX inhibit, so the radio drops its drive. In normal operation the ALC pins sit at 0 V; they do not regulate power.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 ALC (4 V range) Out 0 V normally, about −4 V on a fault 3 ALC (10 V range) Out 0 V normally, about −10 V on a fault 4 TX-INH Out Open drain: switched to GND on a fault

Use the ALC pin that matches your radio's ALC input range: −4 V for most current radios, −10 V for older ones. Check your radio's manual. Wire TX-INH only if your radio has a TX-inhibit input that disables transmit when pulled to GND.

 Controller J24                     Radio

 │ 2 or 3  ALC  ├─────────────────►│ ALC in        │
 │ 4  TX-INH    ├─────────────────►│ TX inhibit in │
 │ 1  GND       ├──────────────────┤ GND           │
 └──────────────┘                  └───────────────┘

docs.title: J16 / J17 · CAT / CI-V
docs.text:
Serial link to the radio for automatic band switching by CAT (two-wire serial) or Icom CI-V (single wire). The logic level is 5 V or 3.3 V, set by solder jumper JP2; match it to your radio or interface. Pin 4 powers a level converter (RS-232 or USB) if you use one.

Warning

Most radios' RS-232 ports use ±12 V levels. Do not connect them directly: use a level converter powered from pin 4.

docs.title: J18 / J19 · Display
docs.text:
Power and the serial link to the ESP32-P4 touch display. The display also passes firmware updates to the controller over this link.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 RX In 3.3 V UART, from display TX 3 TX Out 3.3 V UART, to display RX 4 +5 V Out Display supply 
 Controller J18                     Display
 ┌──────────────┐                  ┌──────────────┐
 │ 4  +5V       ├─────────────────►│ +5V          │
 │ 3  TX        ├─────────────────►│ RX           │

 │ 1  GND       ├──────────────────┤ GND          │

TX goes to RX

Controller TX (pin 3) goes to the display's RX, and controller RX (pin 2) to the display's TX. Some display manufacturers label their connector the other way round, so check the pin-out in your display's manual. See Display and controller not talking.

The display's own CAN port connects to the power supply's CAN bus, where fitted (see the "Other I/O" diagram and CAN bus).

docs.title: J32 / J33 · Rotator
docs.text:
Antenna rotator control: two relay outputs and the position potentiometer. Supports 360° and 450° rotators with 3-point calibration.

Pin Board label Function Notes 1 GND 2 ROT-V Position pot wiper (in) 0 to about 14 V 3 ROT-L CW relay (out) Open drain, switched to GND, 30 V max 4 ROT-R CCW relay (out) Open drain, switched to GND, 30 V max

Pins 3 and 4

On Rev 4.01 the board labels are crossed: pin 3 (ROT-L) turns the rotator clockwise (the >> button), pin 4 (ROT-R) counter-clockwise (<<). Wire by function, not by label. If the rotator turns the wrong way on >>, swap the two wires.

The pot needs its reference voltage from the rotator control box: connect the pot's ends to the box's reference and GND, and the wiper to ROT-V. The calibration works with the pot wired either way round.

docs.title: Firmware and release notes
docs.text:
The controller board and the display each have their own firmware, and both are updated from the browser app over WiFi. Updates are free. Download the latest files from either:

  • the Downloads section of helixrf.com, or
  • the public firmware repository on GitHub: github.com/s21rc/Helixrf-sspa-V4-public.
Board File Example Display display4-vNNN.bin display4-v105.bin Controller controller4-vNNN.bin controller4-v105.bin Controller, USB recovery only controller4-vNNN_full.bin controller4-v105_full.bin

Your settings are kept through updates.

docs.title: Check your versions
docs.text:
Menu → Info shows Display Firmware, Controller Firmware, and the remote head and Neural module versions when they are connected.

The browser app shows the same, and more, under Info: the display build, the remote head link and pair code, the network (hostname, IP address, WiFi network and signal) and the uptime.

Browser app → Info.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
You need the display on WiFi with Enable browser app ticked (menu → Remote). See Network.

  1. Stop transmitting. The update page refuses to start while the amplifier is keyed.
  2. On a PC on the same network, open http://helixrf-sspa4.local/, open the menu (☰) and choose Firmware Update. The top of the page shows the installed versions.
  3. Update the display first, then the controller.

Browser app → Firmware Update.

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
1. Under Display update, choose display4-vNNN.bin (or drop it on the box) and click Upload & install display.
  2. Keep the page open until the upload finishes, then click Reboot now.

The new firmware is written to a spare slot; nothing changes until the display restarts, and the previous firmware stays as a fallback. If the new version misbehaves, the Restore display4-vNNN button (it names the version it goes back to) switches back and restarts the display.

docs.title: Controller
docs.text:
1. Under Controller update, choose controller4-vNNN.bin (not the _full.bin) and click Upload & flash controller.
  2. The amplifier stops for about 15 seconds while the controller is rewritten. The PA is held off and the display shows FIRMWARE UPDATE · DO NOT POWER OFF with a progress bar.
  3. The controller restarts and the display shows the new version.

If the update is interrupted (for example by a power cut), the controller waits in its bootloader: open the page again and click Retry flashing. Restore controller4-vNNN puts back the version that was installed before.

docs.title: Recovering the controller (USB)
docs.text:
Needed only if a controller does not start and the browser update cannot reach it. You need a PC with STM32CubeProgrammer and a USB-C cable.

  1. Switch the 12 V supply on, with the PA supply off.
  2. On the controller board, hold the BOOT0 button, press and release RST, then release BOOT0. The controller is now in its USB bootloader. The two buttons sit side by side above the processor.
  3. Connect the PC to the controller's USB-C port (J34).
  4. In STM32CubeProgrammer, choose USB, click Connect, open controller4-vNNN_full.bin and download it at address 0x08000000.
  5. Press RST. The controller starts with the new firmware, and later updates work from the browser again.

docs.title: Latest · firmware 105
docs.text:
Display and controller firmware 105.

  • Hardware protection on antenna SWR, LPF SWR, output power, drain voltage, drain current and temperature, plus an external drive-overload input, with first-fault indication.
  • RX/TX relay and bias sequencing, with re-arm after faults and power-up.
  • SSB-safe peak-hold PEP and SWR, average power, and 3-point power calibration.
  • Four meter faces: Power Bar, Needle Meter, Large Digit and Power Scope.
  • Automatic band selection by band voltage, BCD, CAT (Yaesu) and CI-V (Icom), with editable per-radio tables, and LPF and antenna maps per band.
  • Current sensing for shunt amplifiers, Hall sensors and BTS high-side switches.
  • Fan control from two NTCs.
  • Antenna rotator with 3-point calibration, 450° support and a GS-232B network server.
  • Eltek Flatpack2 and Emerson eSure power supply control over CAN, with a low-voltage preset.
  • Browser app, remote head and firmware updates for both boards over WiFi.

docs.title: Setup and calibration
docs.text:
Configure the controller for your amplifier, in the order below. Every page is opened from the menu (swipe down on the main screen) and saved with APPLY. Configuration Saved confirms that the controller has stored the settings.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

docs.title: Power module (current sensor)
docs.text:
Menu → Power. Tells the controller how to read the PA current from your High Side Switch or power module, and trims the voltage and current readings.

Three sensor types are supported. Choose the one your module uses in CURRENT SENSOR TYPE, and take its values from the module's manual or the sensor's datasheet. The fields on the page change with the type.

SHUNT+AMPHALL EFFECTBTSx

A shunt resistor with a current-sense amplifier (for example INA240).

Setting Enter REF VOLT (mV) The amplifier's output at zero current. 0 for a unidirectional amplifier. SHUNT (mili Ohm) The shunt resistance in tenths of a milliohm: 10 = 1.0 mΩ. GAIN (V/V) The amplifier's gain, for example 20 for an INA240A1. INVERT MODE Tick if the current reads negative.

Example: an INA240A1 (gain 20) with a 1 mΩ shunt is REF VOLT 0, SHUNT 10, GAIN 20.

A Hall-effect current sensor.

Setting Enter REF VOLT (mV) The sensor's output at zero current, from its datasheet (often half its supply). HALL SENSITIVITY (mV/A) The sensitivity in tenths of a mV/A: 400 = 40.0 mV/A. INVERT MODE Tick if the current reads negative.

A PROFET high-side switch with a current-sense output (BTS50085 class).

Setting Enter K_ILIS The current-sense ratio from the datasheet, for example 13000. R_IS (Ohm) The sense resistor fitted on the module. 0 if none is fitted (the controller's own 10.1 kΩ load is then used).

Calibration (all sensor types): with the PA supply on, compare VOLTAGE (V) and CURRENT (A) with a multimeter. Adjust VOLTAGE CALIBRATION and CURRENT CALIBRATION (percent, 50–150, 100 = no correction) until they match. The readings update as you press the buttons. Tap APPLY.

docs.title: LPF map
docs.text:
Menu → LPF Map. Chooses which of the eight LPF banks (BAND1–BAND8 outputs) each band uses.

Band to LPF map.
  1. Scroll each band's roller to its LPF bank (LPF 1 = BAND1 output, and so on). Bands that share a filter use the same bank.
  2. Tap APPLY.
  3. Check it: tap each band button on the main screen and confirm that the right filter relay clicks.

A wrong LPF map can destroy the PA

Transmitting through a filter for a lower band puts the full output into a filter that reflects it. The LPF SWR trip catches this, but check the map at low power before you run full power on any band.

docs.title: Temperature and fan
docs.text:
Menu → Temperature.

Temperature setting. Setting What it does FAN PWM slider Left handle: the temperature where the fan starts to speed up (it runs at 10 % below it). Right handle: the temperature for full speed. Range 20–65 °C. Invert PWM Tick if the fan runs fast when cold. RESISTANCE (25 °C) Each NTC's resistance at 25 °C, in ohms (10000 for a 10 kΩ NTC). BETA CONSTANT Each NTC's beta value (3950 for the common 10 kΩ type). PROTECTION AT The hardware over-temperature trip point, set by RV5 (read only here). See Protection.

The fan follows whichever NTC is hotter. Tap APPLY, then check both temperatures on the main screen against a thermometer.

docs.title: Protection
docs.text:
Menu → Protection. The trip levels are set with trimmers on the controller board, not in software: the protection works even if the processor stops. This page shows each trimmer's setting as an approximate trip value, so you can set it and record it.

Protection settings. Trimmer Sets Shown on this page as RV1 LPF SWR trip Not shown (see below) RV2 Output power trip (RF OUT) OUTPUT POWER, W RV3 Supply voltage trip DRAIN VOLTAGE, V RV4 Drain current trip DRAIN CURRENT, A RV5 Temperature trip (NTC 1) TEMPERATURE, °C

The antenna SWR trip is fixed at 3:1. Bridge solder jumper JP1 to make it 2:1.

The trip values shown depend on the settings before them: the power trip on the RF power calibration, the current trip on the current sensor, the temperature trip on the NTC values. Set those first. Set RV2 after the RF calibration.

  1. Turn each trimmer until its TRIP VALUE reads the level you want. Set the trips a safe margin above normal operation and below the pallet's ratings:
    • Drain voltage: a few volts above your PA supply voltage.
    • Drain current: above the highest current at full power, below the pallet's maximum.
    • Temperature: below the pallet's maximum heatsink temperature.
    • Output power: above your full output power, below the pallet's and the LPF's rating.
  2. Write the values down for future reference.
  3. Tap APPLY.

LPF SWR (RV1). RV1 sets how much reflection between the PA and the LPF trips the amplifier. Its setting is not shown on the display. More resistance on RV1 makes the trip less sensitive. Set it so that:

  • with the correct filter, the amplifier never trips at full power into a dummy load, and
  • with a wrong filter (map the band to a lower band's bank for the test), it trips at low power.

Info

The trip values on this page are approximate. Comparator offset and the hysteresis resistors shift the real trip point a little. Confirm each trip with the test below.

Enable TX Time out timer (TOT) is reserved for a later firmware and has no effect in firmware 105.

docs.title: RF power calibration
docs.text:
Menu → RF Calibrate. Calibrates the power meter (and the output power trip) at three power levels, against a reference wattmeter.

3-point RF calibration.

You need a dummy load rated for full power and a reference wattmeter between the amplifier and the load. Use a steady carrier (CW key down, FM or RTTY), on the band you use most.

  1. Set the radio to a low drive. Key the amplifier and read the wattmeter: about 20 % of full power.
  2. While transmitting, set LOW · Forward Power Measured to the wattmeter reading with − / + (tap for 1 W, hold for 10 W), then tap the 1 to capture the ADC values. They appear under ADC Value Measured.
  3. Unkey. Repeat at about 50 % power for MID (tap 2) and at full power for HIGH (tap 3).
  4. Tap APPLY.

The three points must increase from LOW to HIGH. The live ADC Value at the top shows the forward and reflected readings while you transmit. Uncalibrated, the power meter reads 0.

docs.title: Rotator
docs.text:
Menu → Rotator.

Rotator setup.
  1. Tick Enable rotator control.
  2. Set CCW stop heading: the compass direction the antenna points to at the counter-clockwise end stop (North, East, South or West).
  3. Tick Enable 450° max AZ if your rotator turns 450°.
  4. Hold << until the rotator reaches its counter-clockwise end stop. Tap APPLY on line 1).
  5. Hold >> for one full turn clockwise (360°). Tap APPLY on line 2).
  6. For a 450° rotator, hold >> to the clockwise end stop. Tap APPLY on line 3).
  7. Tap APPLY at the bottom to save.

On this page the << >> buttons ignore the soft limits, so you can reach the end stops. Rotator ADC shows the live position reading; it must change smoothly as the rotator turns. If >> turns counter-clockwise, swap the relay wires (see J32).

On the main screen, hold << or >> to turn; the rotator stops when you release. For control from a PC program, see Rotator over the network.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
Menu → Diagnose. Live readings of every analog input, for fault finding.

Diagnostics. Column Meaning MCU ADC Raw reading, 0–4095 MCU VALUE Voltage at the processor pin, in mV TRANS VALUE Translated back to the connector, for example the radio's real band voltage before the on-board divider

A reading stuck at 0 usually means an open connection; 4095 with nothing applied means a short to a supply or a wrong wiring. BCD-A to BCD-D show the four BCD inputs as 0 or 1.

docs.title: Test the protection
docs.text:
Test every trip into a dummy load before going on the air, and again after any change to the wiring or the trimmers. Each time, check that the indicator lights, PA RESET turns red, the relay drops and the bias goes off. Then reset with PA RESET.

Trip How to test ANT SWR At low power, transmit into a load above 3:1 (for example 200 Ω, 4:1). LPF SWR At low power, map the band to a lower band's LPF bank and transmit. Restore the LPF map afterwards. RF OUT Turn RV2 down to a low trip (for example 100 W) and transmit above it. Set RV2 back. VOLTAGE With the PA supply on, turn RV3 down until it trips. Set RV3 back. CURRENT Turn RV4 down to a low trip and transmit. Set RV4 back. TEMP. Turn RV5 down to just below the heatsink temperature. Set RV5 back.

After setting a trimmer back, check its value on the Protection page against the value you wrote down.

docs.title: Band data and radio
docs.text: How the controller learns your radio's band, and which antenna each band uses. With automatic band selection the LPF and the antenna follow the radio; in manual you choose the band on the main screen.

docs.title: Choose the method and the radio
docs.text:
Menu → Band Data.

Band Data.

  1. Choose the AUTO BAND SELECTION METHOD:

    Method Radio connection Connector None Manual band selection only Voltage Band-data voltage (Yaesu, Icom ACC) J1 pin 6 BCD 4-line BCD band data (Yaesu) J1 pins 2–5 CAT Serial CAT (Yaesu ASCII) J16 CI-V Icom CI-V J16 pin 3 RF-Sense HelixRF RF sense module; see its manual J1 pin 7

  2. Choose the RIG PROFILE: your radio, or CUSTOM for any other radio.

  3. Tap APPLY.
  4. Open the method's own page from the tiles at the top (VOLTAGE, BCD, CAT/CI-V) and check or enter the band table for your profile.
  5. On the main screen, press and hold AUTO BAND so it lights. Change bands on the radio and check that the amplifier follows.

Built-in profiles:

Profile Methods Notes ICOM IC-7300 Voltage, CI-V CI-V address 94h, 19200 baud YAESU FTDX-10, FT-710 Voltage, BCD, CAT 38400 baud. BCD table preloaded (no code for 60 m and 4 m) CUSTOM All Empty tables: enter your radio's values

Each profile keeps its own band voltage table, BCD table and CAT settings, so you can change radios by changing the profile. A method the profile does not support is greyed out.

Check every band before you rely on it

A wrong table entry does not fail safe: it selects the wrong band, and with it the wrong LPF. Step through every band on the radio at low power and check that the amplifier shows the same band.

docs.title: Band voltage
docs.text:
Band Data → VOLTAGE. Each band has a voltage window: the band is selected while the radio's band-data voltage lies between the two values.

Band voltage setting.
  1. Choose the RIG PROFILE.
  2. On the radio, select a band and read LIVE BAND VOLTAGE (mV): the radio's real band-data voltage, already corrected for the on-board divider.
  3. For that band, set the left value (low limit) a little below the reading and the right value (high limit) a little above it, with − / + (tap for 1 mV, hold for 10 mV). Leave a gap between neighbouring bands.
  4. Repeat for every band. A band with both values at 0 is not used.
  5. Tap APPLY.

docs.title: Band BCD
docs.text:
Band Data → BCD. Each band's BCD code on lines D, C, B and A.

Band BCD setting.
  1. Choose the RIG PROFILE. The Yaesu profile comes with the standard Yaesu table.
  2. On the radio, select a band. LIVE BAND DATA shows the code the radio sends.
  3. Tick the same lines for that band. A band with no line ticked (0000) is not used.
  4. Repeat for every band and tap APPLY.

The BCD inputs are optocoupled, so they accept the radio's band-data levels without loading them.

docs.title: CAT and CI-V
docs.text:
Band Data → CAT/CI-V. The serial settings for the profile.

CAT setting. Setting Enter RIG PROFILE The profile to edit BAUD 1200 to 250000. Must match the radio's CAT or CI-V baud rate. DATA BITS / PARITY / STOP BIT Usually 8, NONE, 1 CI-V ADDRESS The radio's CI-V address (Icom only), for example 94h for the IC-7300 ENABLE CAT PTT Leave off. The amplifier keys only from the wired PTT input.

Tap APPLY. The CAT chip on the main screen lights when the radio answers, and the frequency widget shows the radio's frequency.

On the radio:

  • Icom: set CI-V Transceive to ON, and the CI-V baud rate to the same value as here (not Auto).
  • Yaesu: set the CAT baud rate to the same value as here.

With CAT or CI-V, the link works both ways: tapping a band button on the amplifier also changes the radio's band.

docs.title: Antenna selection
docs.text:
Menu → Antenna. The TX antenna for each band, and whether the band receives on the dedicated RX antenna.

Antenna selection.
  1. For each band, choose the TX antenna, ANT-1 to ANT-4.
  2. Tick RX ANT for bands where you receive on a separate antenna (for example a Beverage on 160 m and 80 m).
  3. Tap APPLY.

The antenna never changes while transmitting. The RX antenna relay is on only while receiving with PA ENABLE on, and drops the instant the amplifier keys, to protect the receiver. With PA ENABLE off, the radio receives on the TX antenna. See J45 for the relay wiring.

docs.title: Network, display and power supply
docs.text: WiFi, the browser app, the remote head, network rotator control, the display settings and the CAN power supply. None of these is needed to operate the amplifier, but WiFi is needed for firmware updates.

docs.title: WiFi
docs.text:
Menu → Network.

Network settings.
  1. Tap SCAN. The networks in range appear on the right.
  2. Tap your network, type the password and tap Connect.
  3. WiFi SSID and IP show the connection, and the WiFi chip on the main screen lights.

The display remembers the network and reconnects at power-up. Disconnect drops it. On your network the amplifier is reachable as http://helixrf-sspa4.local/ (or by the IP address shown).

Enable LAN is reserved and has no effect in firmware 105. To switch WiFi off quickly, use AIRPLANE MODE in Quick Action.

docs.title: Remote
docs.text:
Menu → Remote.

Remote setting. Setting What it does Enable browser app Runs the browser app on your network (needs WiFi). Enable remote display head Lets a HelixRF remote head connect. PAIR appears to approve one.

The choices are saved as soon as you tick them.

docs.title: Browser app
docs.text:
Open http://helixrf-sspa4.local/ on a phone, tablet or PC on the same network. The dot at the top right shows live while the page is connected to the amplifier. The menu (☰) has four pages.

Main: a live copy of the main screen: meters, fault indicators, status chips, temperatures, voltage and current, band buttons, AUTO BAND, rotator, and PA ENABLE and PA RESET (press and hold, as on the display).

Browser app, main page.

Compact View: the same live state in a small panel, without the meters, to keep next to your logging program. Pop out opens it in its own small window. It shows receive or transmit, PA on or off, power, SWR, band and method, antennas, frequency, supply, temperatures and the active fault, with PA ENABLE, PA RESET, a band list and AUTO.

Compact View, popped out.

Firmware Update: see Firmware.

Info: firmware versions, remote head link, network and uptime; see Check your versions.

Every tap goes to the controller through the same path as the touch screen, and the controller applies its usual checks: no band change while transmitting, no reset while a fault is present. Transmit is never possible from the browser: PTT stays on the wired input.

Note

The browser app has no password. Use it only on your own network, and do not forward it to the internet.

docs.title: Remote head
docs.text:
A remote head is a second HelixRF display that mirrors the amplifier over your network, for example on the operating desk while the amplifier sits in another room. It shows and controls everything the main display does.

  1. On the amplifier, tick Enable remote display head.
  2. Connect the remote head to the same WiFi. It shows a four-digit pair code on its own Remote page.
  3. On the amplifier, tap PAIR. A window shows the code of the head that is waiting. If it matches the code on the head in front of you, confirm.

The amplifier remembers the head, so later connections need no approval. The RMT chip lights while the head is connected. To replace the head, tap PAIR with no head waiting and forget the stored one. The remote head's own service page is at http://helixrf-remote4.local/.

docs.title: Rotator over the network
docs.text: While the rotator is enabled, the amplifier runs a Yaesu GS-232B server on TCP port 4001, compatible with the K3NG rotator controller. Set your rotator program (for example PSTRotator or a logging program) to GS-232B over TCP/IP, host helixrf-sspa4.local, port 4001. The ROT chip lights while a program is connected. One program at a time can connect.

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
Menu → Display. These settings are stored in the display.

Display settings. Setting What it does Brightness Backlight, 10–100 %. Changes as you slide. Enable frequency widget Shows the radio frequency (CAT or CI-V) on the main screen. Enable rotator widget Shows the rotator panel on the main screen. Enable clock widget Shows the UTC clock. Display temperature in Fahrenheit °F instead of °C. Enable CPU HUD A small performance overlay, for service. Rotate display Turns the picture 180°, for a display mounted upside down. Takes effect after a restart. Enable PEP hold bar A ghost bar showing the recent peak on the Power Bar face. Default Face The meter face shown at power-up: Power Bar, Needle Meter, Large Digit or Power Scope. Power Scale Full scale of the power meters: 500, 1000, 1500 or 2000 W.

Tap APPLY to keep the settings.

docs.title: CAN bus (power supply)
docs.text:
Menu → CAN Bus. Monitors and sets the voltage of a server power supply on the display's CAN bus.

CAN bus setting.

docs.title: Compatible power supplies
docs.text:
Power supply Output range set from the display Notes Eltek Flatpack2 (48 V HE) 44–57 V Telemetry, default voltage, low-voltage preset Emerson / Vertiv eSure (R48) 42–58 V Telemetry, default voltage (applies at the next power-up)

More supplies will be added in later firmware.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Wire the display's CAN port to the supply's CAN bus (CAN-H to CAN-H, CAN-L to CAN-L, 125 kbit/s), with a twisted pair.

Termination

A CAN bus needs a 120 Ω resistor at each end. The SSPA end is already terminated with 120 Ω. At the power supply end, check whether the supply or its shelf terminates the bus. If not, fit a 120 Ω, 1/4 W resistor between CAN-H and CAN-L at the supply's connector.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Choose the CONNECTED MODULE: ELTEK Flatpack2 or Emerson eSure. The CAN chip on the main screen lights when the bus is live.
  2. The page shows the supply's serial number, AC mains voltage, DC output voltage and current, and its temperatures.
  3. Set DEFAULT VOLTAGE: the output voltage at power-up (Flatpack2: 44–57 V).
  4. Set PRESET LOW VOLTAGE: the voltage that PRESET LOW VOLT in Quick Action switches to (44–48 V, never above the default).
  5. Tap APPLY.

Flatpack2: after APPLY the supply stores the new default. Its telemetry drops out for about 20 seconds, then the output moves to the new voltage.

eSure: the new default is stored in the supply and takes effect when the supply is next powered up.

Warning

Set the default voltage within your pallet's rating. The amplifier's over-voltage trip (RV3) is your backstop; see Protection.

docs.title: Using the controller
docs.text: The main screen, the meter faces, the gestures and what happens when the protection trips.

docs.title: Gestures
docs.text: Gesture On the main screen On the menu or a settings page Swipe down Opens the menu Swipe up Opens Quick Action Goes back Swipe left / right Next / previous meter face Press and hold PA ENABLE, PA RESET, AUTO BAND +/- buttons repeat in steps of 10

docs.title: The main screen
docs.text: Main screen with the needle meter face.

docs.title: Top row
docs.text:
Control What it does PA ENABLE Press and hold to switch the amplifier between operate (bright green) and standby (dark). In standby the RX/TX relay stays in receive and the radio goes straight through. Refused while transmitting. The setting is remembered across power cycles. PA RESET Lights red while the protection is latched. Press and hold to clear the latch and reset external modules. Refused while any fault is still present or while transmitting. Fault indicator Trips when ANT SWR SWR at the antenna bridge exceeds 3:1 (2:1 with JP1 bridged) LPF SWR Reflection between the PA and the LPF is too high: wrong or failed filter RF IN The external drive-overload input (J14 pin 4) is active RF OUT Output power exceeds the RV2 setting VOLTAGE PA supply voltage exceeds the RV3 setting CURRENT Drain current exceeds the RV4 setting TEMP. NTC 1 temperature exceeds the RV5 setting TIMER Reserved for the TX time-out timer

An indicator is red while its fault is present. It turns amber when the fault has cleared but was the cause of a trip that is still latched, so you can see what tripped after the event.

docs.title: Status chips
docs.text:
The small chips at the top right show what is connected.

Chip Lit when CAN Traffic on the display's CAN bus (power supply connected) ROT A rotator program is connected over the network (GS-232B) CAT The radio is answering on CAT or CI-V ALC The protection is latched: ALC pulled down and TX inhibit on WiFi The display is connected to your WiFi RMT A remote head is connected LAN Reserved USB A computer is connected to the display's USB port

docs.title: Meters and readouts
docs.text:
• Power and SWR. Power is shown as PEP (peak hold) or average; SWR is computed from held envelope peaks, so it stays steady on SSB voice. SWR shows -- while receiving. The full scale follows Power Scale in Display settings.
  • VOLTAGE / CURRENT. PA supply voltage and drain current from the High Side Switch.
  • TEMP1 / TEMP2 / FAN. Both NTC temperatures and the fan speed in percent.
  • ROTATOR. Target and current heading, with << and >> to turn the rotator while you hold the button. Shown when the rotator widget is on.
  • TIME (UTC). Set from the internet when the display is on WiFi.
  • Frequency. The radio's frequency, when CAT or CI-V is in use.

docs.title: Band and antenna
docs.text:
The MODE / BAND / TX / RX panel shows the band selection method (MANUAL, BAND-V, BCD, CAT or CI-V), the active band, the TX antenna and the RX antenna (RX ANT when the dedicated receive antenna is in use).

The band buttons at the bottom select a band by hand. The button lights once the controller has switched the LPF and antenna, not before.

AUTO BAND: press and hold to switch between automatic band selection (from your radio) and manual. Not available while transmitting. In manual, the band buttons choose the band; in auto, the radio does. With CAT or CI-V, choosing a band on the amplifier also changes the radio's band.

Note

The band never changes while transmitting. A band you tap during TX is ignored; a band change reported by the radio during TX is applied the moment you unkey.

docs.title: Meter faces
docs.text:
Swipe left or right to change the face. Choose the face shown at power-up in Display settings.

Needle MeterLarge DigitPower BarPower Scope

Analog power and SWR meters. PEP and AVG choose what the power needle shows.

Power and SWR in large digits, readable across the room.

Bar graphs for power and SWR. With PEP hold bar on, a ghost bar marks the recent peak.

A scrolling waveform of the forward power over the last 12 seconds (newest on the right), for checking your keying and speech envelope. The bars run from yellow at the foot to red at the top of the scale, which follows Power Scale.

More faces will be added in later firmware updates.

docs.title: Quick Action
docs.text:
Swipe up on the main screen.

Quick Action. Button What it does AIRPLANE MODE Switches the display's WiFi off, and back on. The browser app, remote head and network rotator control stop while it is on. An aeroplane icon shows on the main screen. PRESET LOW VOLT Drops the power supply to its low-voltage preset (for example for low-power operation or tuning), and back to its default. Needs a compatible power supply on the CAN bus. The PA supply returns to its default after a power cycle.

docs.title: When the protection trips
docs.text:
The comparators trip in nanoseconds and set a hardware latch. The latch, without waiting for the processor:

  • removes the PA bias and pulls the optional gate-kill line to GND,
  • switches the PSU protection lines, so the High Side Switch turns the PA supply off,
  • pulls the radio's ALC down and asserts TX inhibit.

The controller then drops the RX/TX relay and switches PA ENABLE off. The fault indicators show which input tripped.

To recover:

  1. Unkey the radio.
  2. Find and fix the cause: check the antenna, the band and LPF, the drive level and the temperatures.
  3. Wait until no indicator is red (amber is fine).
  4. Press and hold PA RESET. The latch clears, and PA ENABLE returns to what it was before the trip.

If PA RESET does nothing, a fault is still present: its indicator is red. After a reset you have to unkey once before the amplifier keys again, so a PTT that was held through the fault never closes the relay into live drive.
